newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Wesfarmers says wool venture halted.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Wesfarmers says wool venture halted.

text.p: The participants in Global Wool Ltd -- Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd, Futuris Corp unit Elders Ltd and Wool International -- said on Friday they had decided not to proceed with the proposed wool handling and merchandising joint venture.
The participants said in a statement it appeared the chances of implementing the Global Wool proposal, as originally devised, were slim.

The initial proposal, disclosed last October, was for the groups to take over efforts to establish a forward selling market for wool in Australia from Wool International, which is currently responsible for selling the Australian stockpile.

The new company would have offered services to varying sectors of the wool industry, including brokers and buyers, although Elders and Wesfarmers Dalgety would have continued to compete for woolgrowers' business.
Elders and Wesfarmers Dalgety account for about 60 percent of the auction-based movement of wool in Australia.

Australia's competition regulator the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said in May it had advised that the proposal was likely to result in a lessening of competition. An estimated 85 to 95 percent of all Australian wool is currently sold on a spot basis.
Westfarmers managing director John Ring and Elders managing director David Hills said each company would make internal changes to improve wool handling efficiencies.

Both companies would also expand their activities in forward trading and wool price risk management. Global Wool spokesman David Coombes said the deal had collapsed on the commercial difficulties of merging the wool handling arms of Wesfarmers and Elders, rather than on competition factors.

"We were involved in discussions with the ACCC and we were making progress on that," Coombes told Reuters. Although the Global Wool proposal would not proceed, Coombes said he believed there could be other future reforms.
"I think the industry accepts that there has got to be restructuring of the way our wool is handled between the farm and the mill," he said.
The new joint venture had been due to start up on July 1.
